summary_md: **AgentsWatch ([@AgentsWatch](https://x.com/AgentsWatch/status/2115710188745351502))** summarizes *Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong* ([arXiv 2610.37624](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37624)), finding that stripping speaker-attribution tags from shared memory raised group-decision accuracy by 13–24 points on Qwen, Llama and DeepSeek Flash, and that a relevance-first tagged memory reached about 97% on open models (synthetic tasks).

referenced_urls.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions

relevance: Shows how memory formatting shapes multi-agent reasoning quality.

media.description: Bar chart of classic-cell accuracy for Qwen, Llama and Flash comparing tagged, untagged and relevance-first tagged memory (values 54–100%).
